Only data the Terms card cannot supply: a missing rate, value date or ratio stays a refusal on
Calculate (entered on the tab itself).

CalculationBlockerRead.title: CalculationBlockerRead
CalculationBlockerRead.description:
One gap that stops the calculation; ``contract_id`` / ``contract_number`` name the contract it
sits on, both null for a case-level gap (no contract, no agreed loan amount).

CalculationResultResponse.title: CalculationResultResponse
CalculationResultResponse.description:
The calculation result (PRD1042-11, US 1.41, §6.5.8; PRD1042-2266).

The same shape answers the tab's Calculate (a preview, never persisted) and carries the result its
Save stored (``FinancingRead.calculation_result``). ``basis`` records which measurement basis
produced it (only ``present_value`` discounts). All amounts are to the cent.

CalculationStaleCause.title: CalculationStaleCause
CalculationStaleCause.description:
What made the saved calculation out of date (US-1.107, Rule 08 CT8).

Stored on the financing so the Calculations tab can say *why* without reading the audit trail —
a changed contract set reads "The contract set changed. Calculate again." Cleared when a new result
is stored.

CancelCaseRequest.title: CancelCaseRequest
CancelCaseRequest.description:
Cancel a case (US-1.90, Rule 06 §1.5, D1, F3): the reason is mandatory, 1–255 characters, and
is shown in the Activity log. Whitespace-only is refused — a blank reason is no reason.

CaseActivityChange.title: CaseActivityChange
CaseActivityChange.description:
One changed value of an Activity entry, as the viewer may see it (US-1.114, AC5).

`before` / `after` are display values: a user reference is the person's name, a sensitive
value (a bank account) is masked on the server and flagged `masked`. Null reads as "—".

CaseActivityItem.title: CaseActivityItem
CaseActivityItem.description:
One entry in a case's Activity trail (US 1.28 / PRD1042-1944, US-1.114).

A read projection over one audit event. It carries what acted (`actor_type`, and `is_system`
for the System badge), who/which process (`actor_id`/`actor_display`), the role held at the
moment a person acted (`actor_role_at_time`, null for a system actor), what was done
(`event_type` + `entity_display`, the contract number for a contract's entry), why (`reason`),
the changed values (`changes`, masked where sensitive), and when (`recorded_at`, stored UTC).
`old_data` / `new_data` are the event's own data with every sensitive value masked; the FE
reads its sentence parameters from them. Nothing here can be changed — a later event is a new
entry.

CaseActivityResponse.title: CaseActivityResponse
CaseActivityResponse.description: Newest-first, offset-paginated Activity trail for one case.

CaseDataFinancingBlock.title: CaseDataFinancingBlock
CaseDataFinancingBlock.description:
The financing block of the Data area (PRD1042-1938). The terms carriers + the calculation state.
Credit exposure / the financing amount are DERIVED and DEFERRED — reported as pending, never a
computed figure here.

CaseDataResponse.title: CaseDataResponse
CaseDataResponse.description:
The case Data area — the captured data grouped by field block (PRD1042-1938, US 1.22).

Only the blocks whose capture exists today are populated (leasing company, lessee + contracts,
financing, collateral). The blocks whose capture is unbuilt — objects, credit assessment, guarantor
/ co-obligor — are named in ``absent_blocks`` rather than shown empty; the ninth block (1938-OQ-01)
is not built against a guess. Credit exposure is a figure (on the financing block), never a group.

CaseDetailResponse.title: CaseDetailResponse
CaseDetailResponse.description:
The single-case read (``GET /cases/{case_id}``).

Adds the three fields the case header shows and the base response does not carry. They live
here rather than on ``CaseResponse`` because that model is the return of ~10 write endpoints
(create, assign, decide, cancel…) which compute none of this — widening it would make them all
answer null for fields they never looked at, and a null that means "not computed" is
indistinguishable from a null that means "no carrier".

``rate_due_date`` and ``waiting_on_roles`` are also declared on :class:`CaseListItem`. That is
the SECOND occurrence, deliberately left duplicated rather than extracted into a mixin
(`code-quality.md` — note the pattern at two, extract at three); the docs below are kept in
step with it, because the waiting-on null rule is the kind of thing that goes wrong when the
two drift.

CaseDisplayStatus.title: CaseDisplayStatus
CaseDisplayStatus.description:
The single status shown in the list, derived and never stored.

It is not a fourth set: every value here comes from one of the three stored sets. Filtering and
sorting run on the stored sets and never on this value — a query built on a derivation depends
on the derivation instead of on stored data.

CaseDocumentFile.title: CaseDocumentFile
CaseDocumentFile.description:
One file uploaded against a requirement (PRD1042-1939, US 1.23). A requirement holds a SET of
files (a package = many lease contracts against one requirement), each with its own name and
arrival date. The arrival date is stored in UTC and also given in the tenant business timezone
(Europe/Berlin) — no zone label, per the row it belongs to (R6).

CaseDocumentListResponse.title: CaseDocumentListResponse
CaseDocumentListResponse.description:
The case's document list — the resolved requirement set with per-row state and files. Both the
bank and the leasing company (its own obligations) work this one list.

CaseDocumentRow.title: CaseDocumentRow
CaseDocumentRow.description:
One resolved requirement on the case's document list, with its canonical state, its party scope
and its files (PRD1042-1939, US 1.23). Only requirements in the resolved set appear — a type outside
the applicable role scope is absent, never shown as 'not required'.

CaseDuplicateFlag.title: CaseDuplicateFlag
CaseDuplicateFlag.description: An open duplicate pair touching a party of the case — what checklist step 2 lists (US-1.99).

CaseDuplicateFlagParty.title: CaseDuplicateFlagParty
CaseDuplicateFlagParty.description:
One record of an open duplicate pair (US-1.99). ``roles`` is empty when it is not a party of
this case — the bank's other record the case party may duplicate.

CaseDuplicateFlagsResponse.title: CaseDuplicateFlagsResponse
CaseDuplicateFlagsResponse.description: The case's open duplicate flags, bank-only (Rule 06 §2.2.8; Rule 01 — none reach the LC).

CaseLeasingCompaniesResponse.title: CaseLeasingCompaniesResponse
CaseLeasingCompaniesResponse.description:
``GET /cases/leasing-companies`` — rule 02 §1.3 "the leasing companies present in the list"
(BUG-081), sorted by name.

CaseLeasingCompanyOption.title: CaseLeasingCompanyOption
CaseLeasingCompanyOption.description: One leasing company the tenant's cases name (the bank list's Leasing company filter).

CaseLeasingCompanyResponse.title: CaseLeasingCompanyResponse
CaseLeasingCompanyResponse.description:
The leasing company block of a case. Every value is read-only here.

They are changed on the agreement itself, by a Power User, and never from a case. The bank-side
figures are absent for a leasing-company user, which sees its own company and its own agreement
reference and never the bank's numbers.

The two bank accounts are deliberately not here at all. They are partner records the agreement
only designates, they appear on the generated documents, and on this card they are noise.

CaseListItem.title: CaseListItem
CaseListItem.description:
One row of the case list.

**US 1.59 (2026-09-14) settles most of what the docstring below used to defer.** The carriers
the older note was waiting for now exist, so the row carries them instead of leaving the screen
to invent them: the contract and lessee counts come from the contract aggregate, the phase and
the waiting-on role group from the checklist, the rate-due date from the financing. Nothing here
is stubbed — the rule that a zero on a screen reads as a fact still holds, which is why every
added field is nullable and null means "no carrier", never "none".

US-1.77 (Milestone 1 rule 02 §1.1, settling Q-054's two deferred columns): the row names ONE
lessee — the earliest-captured live contract's, with ``lessee_count`` for the "+N" — and the
**initiator role**, the role the case was started under (from the case-started audit entry;
``origin`` stays the channel, for the sub line).

CaseOrigin.title: CaseOrigin
CaseOrigin.description:
How the case came into existence — and, from US 1.4, the request's SUBMISSION CHANNEL.

PRD1042-1920 (US 1.4) names four carriers of "where the data actually came from" on the request:
portal, bank-internal, bulk file, and the migration container marker saying migrated with no
process performed. **This enum IS that field.** It is extended rather than joined by a second
``submission_channel`` column: two columns carrying the same fact drift, and one of them then
silently becomes the wrong answer. The mapping is:

* ``PORTAL``   — the leasing company submitted through the portal (a case nobody in the bank has
  checked yet, which is why it arrives unowned in the Front Office work list).
* ``WIZARD``   — **bank-internal.** The channel named "bank-internal" on the spec's field table is
  exactly the guided wizard a bank user drives; ``WIZARD`` predates the 1920 wording and is kept
  rather than renamed, because the stored value is already in the database and a rename buys
  nothing over this note.
* ``BULK_FILE`` — the request was filled from an uploaded contract file (US 1.5 / PRD1042-1921
  owns the import itself; this value is only the channel marker it stamps).
* ``MIGRATED`` — the container-request marker: the migration creates one request per migrated
  package with no process performed, so an empty checklist and an empty approval history on it
  are legitimate rather than incomplete.

The channel is **system-set, never caller-supplied** (spec: "Req. — System"). No HTTP schema
accepts it: ``CaseService.create_case`` derives it from who is acting. That is what keeps an
ordinary wizard request from presenting itself as a migration container and borrowing its
excuse for an empty checklist and approval history.

Distinct from ``Contract.contract_origin``: this is the channel the *request* arrived by, while
that one is the marker an individual *contract* carries (needed to reconcile a bulk run's error
report against what actually landed). Deliberately two fields rather than one — a request filled
by several runs plus hand entry has ONE channel and contracts of DIFFERING origins.

CasePartyMatchResponse.title: CasePartyMatchResponse
CasePartyMatchResponse.description:
The case's parties + their match outcomes and advisory duplicate flags (PRD1042-1929, US-1.86).

A duplicate never holds the submission (Milestone 1 rule 03 §5.4), so the response carries no
case-level block signal — the bank-side gate reads the per-party flags.

CasePrimaryEntity.title: CasePrimaryEntity
CasePrimaryEntity.description:
Which of a case's three status carriers is the one that governs its display (US 1.49).

The primary-entity rule (`derive_display_status`) reads the finest available carrier — the
financing outranks the request, the request outranks the case. This enum names WHICH carrier won,
so the interface can label the shown status with the record it belongs to (a "Financing" /
"Request" / "Case" strip) without re-deriving the rule on the client. It is derived on read from
the same inputs as the display status and never stored.

CaseProductTemplateResponse.title: CaseProductTemplateResponse
CaseProductTemplateResponse.description:
The product rules, visible while contracts are entered.

Only the confirmed bound is here. The allowed object categories and the min/max volume are not
confirmed product bounds (1919-OQ-02, 1919-OQ-01) and are absent rather than shown empty, which
would read as "none configured".

CaseProgressResponse.title: CaseProgressResponse
CaseProgressResponse.description: A case's phase-grouped checklist progress + overall roll-up (US-1.18).

CaseReviewResponse.title: CaseReviewResponse
CaseReviewResponse.description:
The one-page review of a refinancing request before submission (PRD1042-1933, US 1.17).

Everything entered, on one page: the case, the leasing company + agreement values, every contract
with its lessee / type / residual and completeness, the collateral, and the financing figures (the
volume pending). A read projection composing the existing per-concern reads — each block keeps its
own visibility rule (an LC user sees the LC block blanked of bank figures, and nothing the rate went
into). Blocks not captured yet are null: a draft under review is incomplete by nature.

CaseStatus.title: CaseStatus
CaseStatus.description: The case's own state. One of the three sets the display status is derived from.

CaseType.title: CaseType
CaseType.description:
PRD1042-1917 OQ-01 (closed 19 Aug 2026) — the seven case types, and the process each runs.

All seven carry a checklist, with the catalogue step counts recorded on the ticket: main
process 44, package redemption 20, single redemption 11, lessee change 8, object swap 8,
asset event 4, extension 42. The earlier figure of six belongs to 17 Aug, when the extension
was still held back; it was released on 18 Aug and is one case with its own catalogue, not two.

Amendment Request is deliberately absent: the CrossLease click dummy offers it, the client does
not have it, and it is not built. The Financing is not a case type either — it has actions
rather than a workflow, and it cannot own a catalogue.

CatalogCaseTypeItem.title: CatalogCaseTypeItem
CatalogCaseTypeItem.description:
PRD1042-1790 item 1 — a case type that may own a catalogue, and the entity type it derives.

Exists so no client has to carry its own copy of ``TYPED_CASE_TYPES``. AC-94 refuses an
implementation "wired to a fixed count of case types", and an enum the FE re-lists is exactly
that: assigning a catalogue to a third case type would need a frontend release. Reading the set
from here makes it a backend change, and later a configuration one, with no client work.

``entity_type`` is the coarse object the case type derives (``CASE_TYPE_ENTITY_TYPE``). It is not
part of the create contract — the backend derives it — and is surfaced only so a client can label
or group by it without re-deriving the mapping. It is null for the case types that derive no
entity type (since PRD1042-1917 not every case type maps to one).

CatalogState.title: CatalogState
CatalogState.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 8 (AC §7) — the catalogue lifecycle: Draft → Active → Suspended.

A new catalogue starts DRAFT (never resolved by a case). Activation runs the validator and, on
success, makes it the one resolved for its case type + product. An Active catalogue can be
suspended (stops resolving for new cases; nothing deleted) and reactivated. Editing is in place on
any state — the audit trail is the history (no version flow). ARCHIVED is a reserved post-MVP
terminal (not reachable through this flow).

collateral_type.description: Manual capture accepts GUARANTEE, SECURITY_DEPOSIT and BUY_BACK_AGREEMENT only; the other members are MILK-import types (422 here).

CollateralAddRequest.title: CollateralAddRequest
CollateralAddRequest.description:
Add a collateral to a contract (PRD1042-2167).

A party (``identity`` to create-confirmed, or ``existing_partner_id`` to link an existing one) is
given ONLY for a ``GUARANTEE`` — the service rejects a party on the other types, and requires
exactly one for a Guarantee. ``value`` is mandatory (US-1.84, rule 04 §4.3).

Every type except ``GUARANTEE`` names its **provider** instead (rule 04 C2): ``provider_name`` is
mandatory there and the address optional; a Guarantee refuses them, its partner is the provider.
There is no "kind of obligation" (rule 04 C4): a Guarantee's guarantor link always records
``guarantee``.

``collateral_type`` is one of the three MANUAL types only — ``GUARANTEE``, ``SECURITY_DEPOSIT``,
``BUY_BACK_AGREEMENT`` (P30-05); the five MILK-only types answer 422 here and arrive through the MILK
import alone.

A Guarantee party created here also takes its OS+ number and the party mask's addresses and
dealer numbers (``NewPartyExtras``, P30-17) — refused without ``identity``.

CollateralDecisionBlock.title: CollateralDecisionBlock
CollateralDecisionBlock.description:
Why a caller may not approve or reject an open DAT re-determination (P29-06, hub Q-105) — shown
beside the proposal instead of the buttons. The same rule refuses the approval itself.

CollateralEvidenceItem.title: CollateralEvidenceItem
CollateralEvidenceItem.description: One DAT evidence file (US-1.112) — DAT PDF or vehicle Excel, on the DAT card only (DA4).

CollateralListItem.title: CollateralListItem
CollateralListItem.description: One live collateral on a contract, for the summary. A Guarantee row carries its party's name.

CollateralListResponse.title: CollateralListResponse
CollateralListResponse.description: The collaterals a contract carries and how many (PRD1042-2167). Empty is normal, not incomplete.

CollateralPreviewRequest.title: CollateralPreviewRequest
CollateralPreviewRequest.description: Search the partner register for a Guarantee's party before creating — the identity to match on.

CollateralProvider.title: CollateralProvider
CollateralProvider.description: Who provides a non-Guarantee collateral (rule 04 C2). Null on a Guarantee and on older rows.

CollateralRecheckState.title: CollateralRecheckState
CollateralRecheckState.description:
The re-check flag on a financing's DAT total (PRD1042-1930 R2; P29-06; the PO's DAT spec §5.3).

A PROMPT, not a gate — it blocks no step (no step-28 block):

* ``NEEDS_RECHECK`` — raised by a settled redemption that leaves at least one contract (the only
  raiser — P30-44);
* ``CLEAR``         — never raised, or cleared by an APPROVED re-determination (the only way).

A proposed re-determination is not a state of the flag: it is ``proposed_total_eur`` on the record,
and its approval or rejection leaves the flag as the rule above says (the retired ``redetermined``
value was folded into ``needs_recheck`` by migration ``fin3044flag01``).

CollateralRemoveRequest.title: CollateralRemoveRequest
CollateralRemoveRequest.description:
Soft-remove a collateral — history preserved. The reason is optional while the request is Draft
and required after it (rule 04 C3, the same rule as a contract removal); 422
``COLLATERAL_REMOVAL_REASON_REQUIRED`` otherwise.

CollateralType.title: CollateralType
CollateralType.description:
What kind of security backs the package (PRD1042-1930, US 1.14).

Three confirmed values, a SINGLE selection for now. The platform records the kind — it neither
values collateral nor holds a register of it. Whether a package can carry more than one kind at
once is undecided (1930-OQ-03); the model does not foreclose that answer (a single column now, a
join table can supersede it later without reshaping the record). No type or registration sub-enum
is built — that is a later phase.

CollateralValueItem.title: CollateralValueItem
CollateralValueItem.description:
One version of the DAT total — the first value, or an approved re-determination (by its
proposer).

CommentRefType.title: CommentRefType
CommentRefType.description:
P29-01 — what a comment thread hangs on (prototype 29 Sep, ``activityAndComments``).

A case's thread is the bank ↔ leasing-company correspondence (US 1.53, US-1.113). A financing's, a
party's and a contract's threads are **bank-only**: the leasing company has no path to either, so their comments
are always ``CommentVisibility.INTERNAL`` and never reach the LC read paths or its notifications.

CommentVisibility.title: CommentVisibility
CommentVisibility.description:
Who a case comment is for (PRD1042-1951 / US 1.53 part 1, PO answer A4 2026-09-11).

The thread was built as one shared record — its model docstring still reads "One thread, both
sides see all of it". That is what this enum ends: a comment now names its audience, and the
leasing company never receives an ``INTERNAL`` one.

**``INTERNAL`` is the default.** Per A4 the bank writes internally unless it deliberately
chooses otherwise — making a comment external is an explicit user action, so the safe value is
the one that does not reach the customer by accident. Note this is the opposite of the BACKFILL
default: rows written before this field existed were genuinely shared correspondence the LC has
already read, so the migration sets them ``EXTERNAL`` rather than retroactively hiding history.

Enforced at query level in ``CaseCommentService.list_comments`` — A4 is explicit that the
restriction is a system-level one, not something the interface hides.

ConditionOperator.title: ConditionOperator
ConditionOperator.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 7 (AC §6) — the six operators a display-condition row may use. The offered
set follows the field type (enforced at the FE; not restricted server-side in this store-only slice).

ContractCollateralType.title: ContractCollateralType
ContractCollateralType.description:
The kind of collateral securing a leasing contract (PRD1042-2167, unblocks US 1.45).

A **contract-scoped** set, deliberately SEPARATE from the case-level ``CollateralType``
(``cases/domain/enums.py`` — ``chattel_mortgage`` / ``assignment_of_receivables`` / ``guarantee``).
The two levels are NOT merged: these values come from position 20d of the application form, which is
contract level, and the PO's 2026-09-14 answer (Q-044) fixed this set without converging it upstream.

- ``GUARANTEE`` — a partner stands behind the contract. This is the ONE type that captures a party:
  the user selects/creates a Partner (the lessee's search-or-create flow) and the platform assigns
  that partner the **guarantor role** on the contract (a ``contract_guarantor`` link). Guarantor is
  therefore a role DERIVED from a Guarantee collateral, never captured on its own — which is what
  lets the standalone Guarantors tab retire (US 1.45).
- ``SECURITY_DEPOSIT`` / ``BUY_BACK_AGREEMENT`` — value-only, no party captured.

(The prototype's ``RKV`` dropdown entry is NOT a member — per Q-044 it is a prototype error; RKV
survives only as a Yes/No contract field and as document type REQ-004, both owned elsewhere.)

``SCREAMING_SNAKE`` member, ``SCREAMING_SNAKE`` value — the wire vocabulary is fixed and glossary-
binding, so unlike the proposal-stage contract-terms enums this one is safe to constrain in the DB
(a CHECK on the column, ``enums-and-constants.md``).

ContractCompleteness.title: ContractCompleteness
ContractCompleteness.description:
Whether a contract carries enough captured data to be submitted (PRD1042-1928).

Derived on read, never stored (see ``domain/completeness.py``): a contract is ``COMPLETE`` when its
required fields are present and ``INCOMPLETE`` otherwise, and the request cannot be submitted while
any active contract is incomplete. Storing it would be a second carrier that drifts from the data it
is derived from.

ContractCreate.title: ContractCreate
ContractCreate.description:
The fields accepted when adding a contract. ``batch_id`` is the import run the contract came from
(US-1.5); a hand-added contract omits it.

ContractDefer.title: ContractDefer
ContractDefer.description:
Why a committed contract leaves the package (C-8, BUG-097) — required then, ignored before the
step-4 decision, when deferring is a reversible hold within the review.

ContractDeferredState.title: ContractDeferredState
ContractDeferredState.description:
Whether a contract is live in the request or held back (PRD1042-1928).

A deferred contract is set aside within the request — reactivatable, **not** rejected. It stays
part of the request's history and can be brought back into the active set; it simply does not count
toward the active package while deferred, and (per the spec) carries no financing component while
held back. The default for a newly added contract is ``ACTIVE``.

ContractEdit.title: ContractEdit
ContractEdit.description:
The editable fields of an existing contract.

Provenance is not editable and is not accepted here: ``batch_id`` (which delivery) is set once when
the contract is created, and ``contract_origin`` (where it came from, PRD1042-1920) is a System field
with an open value set (1920-OQ-01) that no caller supplies. Both are read-only on ``ContractRead``.

ContractEditLock.title: ContractEditLock
ContractEditLock.description: Why (part of) a contract cannot be edited — the narrowest lock that applies.

ContractFilterOption.title: ContractFilterOption
ContractFilterOption.description:
One value a contract-list dropdown offers (P30-15). ``label`` is the display text; for the
Refinancing status it is the code, which the client translates.

contract_origin.title: Contract Origin
contract_origin.description: Where this contract came from, for reconciling a bulk run's error report against what actually landed. Read-only and system-set. Free-form on purpose: the value set is open on the client side (1920-OQ-01), so no allowed values are documented or enforced yet.

ContractListItem.title: ContractListItem
ContractListItem.description:
A contract as the intake wizard's step-2 list renders it (BUG-044 item 2).

``ContractRead`` plus the two figures that row displays and the contract record does not hold:
the lessee's NAME (a partner reference) and how many LIVE lease objects it carries (their own
rows). The click dummy's table is *"Contract / lessee · Term · Objects"*, and neither the name
nor the count could be rendered without one request per row.

Extends ``ContractRead`` rather than restating it — same reasoning as ``ContractWorkSurfaceItem``
above, which is a sibling of this shape for the cross-case surface. It stays separate from
``ContractRead`` so the four single-contract endpoints do not have to resolve two values they
never display, and so neither field is ever present-but-unpopulated.

ContractListResponse.title: ContractListResponse
ContractListResponse.description: One bounded page of a request's contracts plus the total matching the filter.

contract_origin.title: Contract Origin
contract_origin.description: Where this contract came from, for reconciling a bulk run's error report against what actually landed. Read-only and system-set. Free-form on purpose: the value set is open on the client side (1920-OQ-01), so no allowed values are documented or enforced yet.

ContractRead.title: ContractRead
ContractRead.description:
A contract row, with its derived completeness (PRD1042-1928).

``completeness`` and ``missing_fields`` are derived on read (``domain/completeness.py``), never
stored: the badge and its reasons follow the current data. ``deferred_state`` is the live/held-back
state; ``removed_at`` + ``removal_reason`` are present on a soft-removed row (history preserved).

``batch_id`` + ``contract_origin`` are the provenance pair a bulk run's error report is reconciled
against (PRD1042-1920): which delivery the row came in on, and where it came from. Both are
read-only here — see ``contract_origin`` below and ``ContractEdit``.

ContractRecordEditable.title: ContractRecordEditable
ContractRecordEditable.description: P30-08 — the freeze points for this caller and contract (``domain/write_window.py``).

ContractRecordFigures.title: ContractRecordFigures
ContractRecordFigures.description: P30-07 — the Overview's counts, over the contract's live objects and collaterals.

ContractRecordRead.title: ContractRecordRead
ContractRecordRead.description:
P30-06 — one contract as its record page reads it (`GET /contracts/{id}`).

Own contracts only: a leasing-company caller reaches only its own company's contracts (the scope
is in the query), and another company's id answers 404 like an unknown one. For the portal the
``financing`` and ``framework_agreement`` are always null — the approved prototype shows neither
there (working assumption, Q-115); the portal's Loan payment plan gets its own scoped read (P30-10).

ContractRecordRef.title: ContractRecordRef
ContractRecordRef.description: A record the contract page names and links: its id and its display name (null when unnamed).

ContractRemove.title: ContractRemove
ContractRemove.description:
Why a contract is removed — optional while the request is Draft, required after submission
(rule 08 §3.2, US-1.106); preserved with the soft-removed record.

ContractShareRead.title: ContractShareRead
ContractShareRead.description:
P30-51 — one contract's share of the payout. The percentages of a financing add up to exactly 100.00 %
(largest remainder, in hundredths of a percent).

ContractStatus.title: ContractStatus
ContractStatus.description:
The contract's own lifecycle status (US-1.56 — the cancellation cascade).

Distinct from ``ContractDeferredState`` (live vs held-back within an open request) and from the
soft-delete carriers (``removed_at`` / ``removal_reason``): this is the terminal lifecycle marker a
contract carries when its parent case is cancelled. The 44-step matrix's lease-contract value set did
not carry ``Cancelled`` (it lists Draft…Closed); the PO's cancellation-cascade decision (Additional
Notes, 2026-09-11) adds it — every contract of a cancelled case moves to ``CANCELLED`` as a stored
status, not a derivation. The default for a live contract is ``ACTIVE``.

BUG-051 added the matrix's remaining seven values so the Workflow Task Catalog can author them as
completion targets. Note ``DEFERRED`` here is the contract's LIFECYCLE status and is a different
fact from ``ContractDeferredState.DEFERRED``, which says whether a live contract is held back
within an open request. They share a word and a column they will never share.

BUG-097 — a contract starts ``SUBMITTED`` ("Submitted at the point the bank starts work", 44-step
matrix) and moves along the matrix's C-edges below. ``ACTIVE`` is kept only as the value rows held
before migration ``ctr097life01``; it has no edge, so nothing moves into or out of it.

ContractType.title: ContractType
ContractType.description:
The kind of leasing contract (PRD1042-1925, US 1.9).

``LEASE`` is Leasing, ``HIRE_PURCHASE`` is Mietkauf. The contract type selects which of the two
contract documents (``Leasingvertrag`` / ``Mietkaufvertrag``) is the required one — exactly one per
case (PRD1042-1794). Mandatory before the bank settlement, not at submission (the draft saves
without it). ``LEASE`` / ``HIRE_PURCHASE`` are a client-side *proposal* for the code names, not yet

Kilometerleasing (the mileage flag) are separate facts, NOT contract types.

ContractWorkSurfaceItem.title: ContractWorkSurfaceItem
ContractWorkSurfaceItem.description:
One row of the standalone Contracts list (US-1.73, P30-15).

Deliberately NOT ``ContractRead``: that is the per-case detail shape, and this row carries what it
does not — the lessee's NAME, the case's REFERENCE, the first object and the financing, all
resolved once per page. A cross-case list that showed a lessee id and a case uuid would be
unreadable.

CorrectSettlementRequest.title: CorrectSettlementRequest
CorrectSettlementRequest.description:
Correct a settlement before SetUp, returning the financing to Calculating (US 1.42, D-144).

The correction is a real, expected case — but it must say WHY: the reason is mandatory and rides the
audit entry (§5.8.8). Whitespace-only is rejected (a blank reason is no reason).

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Optional module keys to activate beyond always-on

DATEvidenceStatus.description:
The DAT evidence state on a vehicle object (PRD1042-1924).

Held as **status + upload only** — a DAT value per object is NOT stored (the collateral total sits
on the package, PRD1042-1930). ``PENDING`` once the capture step is opened, ``UPLOADED`` once the
document reference is recorded. A separate approval/verification state belongs to the collateral /
document model, not here — kept to the two states this story owns.

DashboardResponse.title: DashboardResponse
DashboardResponse.description:
The bank dashboard (US-1.71) — what is moving through refinancing today.

Composed server-side from the case and financing lists. The counts are over the whole visible
SET, not over a page: a dashboard that counted a page would report the page.

``financed_volume_eur`` is always null today and says so in its own field rather than by being
absent — the click dummy sums a payout per financing and no payout field exists (the financings

not as zero and not as an em dash: a dash on this card would claim the bank financed nothing.

effective_from.description: Deactivation date — past/now for immediate, future for scheduled

DecideRequestRequest.title: DecideRequestRequest
DecideRequestRequest.description:
The approver's decision on a submitted refinancing request (PRD1042-1945, US 1.29).

One endpoint, the outcome in the body — not four per-outcome routes. ``outcome`` is one of the
four decision values of ``RequestStatus`` (commit / reject / missing-information / rework); a
value outside that set (e.g. ``draft`` / ``submitted``, or an unknown string) is rejected at the
boundary as a 422 validation error. ``reason`` is mandatory for reject + missing-information
(enforced in the service so every future client inherits the rule) and optional otherwise.

DirectDebitReturnCreate.title: DirectDebitReturnCreate
DirectDebitReturnCreate.description:
P30-13 — record a direct debit return (M2 spec §4.6). No amount: a return concerns the whole
instalment, named by its due date (a paid row of the lease cash flow).

DirectDebitReturnRead.title: DirectDebitReturnRead
DirectDebitReturnRead.description:
P30-13 — one return: the instalment, both statements (reported by the leasing company, recorded
by the bank — who and when) and, once resolved, when the payment came in.

DirectDebitReturnReason.title: DirectDebitReturnReason
DirectDebitReturnReason.description:
P30-13 — why a lessee's direct debit came back. The client's list (Laurence, 1 Oct; M2 spec §4.6),
which replaces the five values of the approved build. ``OTHER`` carries a description.

DirectDebitReturnResolve.title: DirectDebitReturnResolve
DirectDebitReturnResolve.description: P30-13 — resolve an open return: when the payment came in, and an optional note.

DirectDebitReturnStatus.title: DirectDebitReturnStatus
DirectDebitReturnStatus.description:
P30-13 — a recorded return is ``OPEN`` (the instalment is not paid) until it is ``RESOLVED`` (the
payment came in); a resolved return stays in the history.

DiscountingRowResponse.title: DiscountingRowResponse
DiscountingRowResponse.description: One row of the Derivation's fold "Discounting payment by payment" (Rule 07 §7, US-1.101).

DocumentCheckMark.title: DocumentCheckMark
DocumentCheckMark.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 6 (AC §5, Laurence 12 Aug) — the single mark set, the same for every check
on every step (nothing to configure per check). Recorded per check at runtime; the catalogue only
defines the checks. Two paper-form values fall away deliberately (vorhanden dropped; nicht

DocumentManagedOn.title: DocumentManagedOn
DocumentManagedOn.description: Where a row shown in the table is edited instead — the table never edits it.

DocumentOverrideKind.title: DocumentOverrideKind
DocumentOverrideKind.description:
CR PRD1042-1794 A3 — the per-leasing-company override, held on the Framework Agreement as two
sets. `ADDITIONALLY_REQUIRED` adds a document type to the resolved set for that LC;
`NOT_REQUIRED` removes one from it. The standard set is never stored on the FA — reading the FA
alone gives only the deviation.

DocumentRoleScope.title: DocumentRoleScope
DocumentRoleScope.description: Which party a document concerns (13 Aug: every registry type carries one).

DocumentRowRead.title: DocumentRowRead

DocumentRowType.title: DocumentRowType
DocumentRowType.description: The table's Type column — document type codes (Dev B's choice for the object's DAT report: ``DAT_REPORT``).

DocumentTypeMatrixResponse.title: DocumentTypeMatrixResponse
DocumentTypeMatrixResponse.description: CR-DRC B9: the bank's document matrix, GENERATED from the registry (not maintained as a grid).

DocumentTypeOrigin.title: DocumentTypeOrigin
DocumentTypeOrigin.description:
Registry mark (B9/B10): the 32 catalogue types are all `requested`; the 7 named documents the
platform produces are `generated`. Drives the B10 compatibility rule — an upload task may reference
only a `requested` type, a generate task only a `generated` type.

DuplicateCheckStatus.title: DuplicateCheckStatus
DuplicateCheckStatus.description:
Decided internally 1 Oct: the prototype shows only "clear"; a check also needs its negative
result. The app does not run the check — no source says what it compares (Q-109).

DuplicateKeepApartRequest.title: DuplicateKeepApartRequest
DuplicateKeepApartRequest.description: Keep the two apart — they are different parties (P30-25). The note is optional.

DuplicateMergeRequest.description:
Merge in the chosen direction (P30-25): ``survivor_partner_id`` stays, the other record is
retired and its roles and references move to the survivor. No reason code; the note is optional.

DuplicatePairResolutionResponse.title: DuplicatePairResolutionResponse
DuplicatePairResolutionResponse.description: The pair and both of its records — the resolution dialog's survivor cards and merge preview.

EditCaseCommentRequest.title: EditCaseCommentRequest
EditCaseCommentRequest.description:
US-1.61 — the author rewrites their own comment's body. Visibility is not editable here (it is
an audience decision fixed at authoring); only the text changes.

ExcludedPaymentResponse.title: ExcludedPaymentResponse
ExcludedPaymentResponse.description: A lease payment left out of the refinanced stream, with the reason (§6.5.8).

FAAgreementLifecycle.title: FAAgreementLifecycle
FAAgreementLifecycle.description:
The *derived* agreement-level lifecycle. Computed from the anchor's stored status + termination
stamp + validity — never stored. `EXPIRED` is a past `valid_until` on an otherwise-active
agreement; `TERMINATED` is the terminal, agreement-level end. `DEACTIVATED` is the switched-off
state (PRD1042-1891 §3) and takes precedence over EXPIRED. (CR-FA-04 versioning withdrawn.)

FALinkedFinancingItem.title: FALinkedFinancingItem
FALinkedFinancingItem.description:
BUG-141 — one financing drawn under the agreement, as the approved prototype's card shows it (reference,
kind, contract count, payout amount, status). Bank-only: the route answers 404 to everyone else.

FALinkedFinancingsResponse.title: FALinkedFinancingsResponse
FALinkedFinancingsResponse.description: BUG-141 — the financings drawn under one agreement, newest first, paged. ``count`` is the total.

FAPinnedVersionChangeImpact.title: FAPinnedVersionChangeImpact
FAPinnedVersionChangeImpact.description:
PRD1042-1891 §1 — a pinned-version change identifies what it affects (no auto re-pin). One entry
per template whose pinned BPT version changed on this edit. Downstream counts are stubs until the
Financing epic; the structure is fixed now so the FE knows what to expect.

FAPricingSnapshotResponse.title: FAPricingSnapshotResponse
FAPricingSnapshotResponse.description:
Pricing snapshot returned to consuming epics (US 11.11).

Epic 3 (Financing) uses edit_version_counter as the audit anchor
to reconstruct which FA pricing snapshot was applied at Stage 2 approval.

FinancingBalanceRead.title: FinancingBalanceRead
FinancingBalanceRead.description:
The balance banner, read off the stored calculation. Every figure is null until one is stored.

``outstanding`` is the closing balance of the repayment schedule's row due on or before today —
null until the payout (P29-04). ``provisional`` holds until the rate is committed at the
commitment step — the prototype's "Provisional until the case reaches Committed stage".
Before P30-38 ``payout`` fell back to the agreed loan amount; that figure is now
``approved_loan_amount``, so the banner and the list read one payout.

FinancingComponentResponse.title: FinancingComponentResponse
FinancingComponentResponse.description:
A contract's share of the financing. The share figures are deferred (nullable) — the calc engine
populates them (1931-OQ-03); the component carries the plan + the calculation date now.

FinancingDetailRead.title: FinancingDetailRead
FinancingDetailRead.description: One financing by its own id (P29-02): the financing plus its page header and tab counts.

FinancingDocumentType.title: FinancingDocumentType
FinancingDocumentType.description:
P29-07 — the document type a financing's miscellaneous document is classified as (the
prototype's picker: Original agreement · Addendum · Correspondence · Other). Optional on upload —
a document may sit unclassified until someone sets it.

FinancingEndedReason.title: FinancingEndedReason
FinancingEndedReason.description:
Why a financing reached ``ENDED`` (PRD1042-1952, US 1.36).

``ENDED`` is the planned end of a financing, not a failure — the reason records *how* it ended, and
is set **only** on the transition into ``ENDED`` (the transition engine requires it there and
forbids it everywhere else). The three ways a financing ends per the state matrix:

* ``TERM_RAN_OUT`` — the last contract reached the end of its agreed term (the ordinary end);
* ``TERMINATED`` — the financing was terminated before term;
* ``REDEEMED_EARLY`` — the outstanding amount was repaid early.

Member ``SCREAMING_SNAKE``, value lowercase — the same StrEnum idiom as ``FinancingKind`` /
``FinancingStatus`` (``enums-and-constants.md``: the wire value is what crosses the boundary).

FinancingFilterOptionsResponse.title: FinancingFilterOptionsResponse
FinancingFilterOptionsResponse.description: P29-15 — the values one list dropdown offers, narrowed by ``q``, capped (see the route).

FinancingKind.title: FinancingKind
FinancingKind.description:
Whether the financing redeems one contract or a package of them (PRD1042-1948).

A single financing redeems exactly one leasing contract; a package financing redeems several under
one refinancing. The value is provisional at intake — US-1.16 (PRD1042-1932) derives it from the
contract count once the contract model exists (US 1.6/1.8/1.12). Until then the financing is created
as ``SINGLE`` (see the model's ``kind`` column note).

FinancingListItem.title: FinancingListItem
FinancingListItem.description:
One row of the standalone financings list (PRD1042-1949, US 1.33; widened by US-1.65).

P29-15 added the loan account and the Sollbelastung / Habenausgleich amounts (kept by hand since
P29-03) and ``outstanding``, the row highlight of the prototype's Outstanding toggle.

P30-38 added ``payout_amount``: the stored calculation's disbursement, null before the first
calculation (``application/payout.py`` — the detail banner reads the same figure).

US-1.66 added ``account_no`` (Q-113): the IBAN of the payout account the financing's framework agreement
designates — never typed on the financing, never from OS+; every financing under one agreement shares it.

FinancingRead.title: FinancingRead
FinancingRead.description:
The financing a committed refinancing request has come into existence as (PRD1042-1948).

Read-only. There is no create or update surface — a financing is never created by hand, only as the
outcome of committing a request. Bank-internal: a leasing-company user never receives it (1948-R4).

FinancingSecuritiesResponse.title: FinancingSecuritiesResponse
FinancingSecuritiesResponse.description:
P29-06 — the Collaterals tab's "Collaterals" card: every live collateral on the financing's
contracts. Read only — they are captured with the contract.

FinancingSecurityItem.title: FinancingSecurityItem
FinancingSecurityItem.description: P29-06 — one collateral captured on a contract of the financing, with that contract.

FinancingStatus.title: FinancingStatus
FinancingStatus.description:
The financing's state.

Defined here because the derived display status reads it, **not** because the case stores it.
No financing status column is added to the case — the financing owns its own state, and a
second carrier here would drift from it.

`DRAFT` is the entry state of the nine-value model formalised at PO level on 10 Sep 2026 (the
44-step matrix v1.1, hub Q-024): a financing is created with the case and starts in `Draft`, and
the primary-entity rule reads it (`Financing.status = Draft` → the Refinancing Request is primary).
The financing is minted in `DRAFT` with the refinancing request (`FinancingService.
create_draft_for_request`, PRD1042-2266), per the PO answers on hub Q-042: created at request
creation, `kind` derived later at the commit, and the Draft survives a reject / missing-information
/ rework decision — only a case cancel ends it. A-3 moves it to `CALCULATING` at the commit.

`ENDED` is the planned end of a financing, not a failure. `CANCELLED` (PRD1042-1952, US 1.36) is
a state of the financing, not merely an action: cancellation *is* a financing state per the state
matrix, reachable from any non-terminal state, and terminal like `ENDED`. It lives here for the
same reason every other financing status does — the derived display status reads it, and a second
carrier would drift. The allowed transitions between these states are defined once, in
`financing/domain/transitions.py` (the single source of truth for legality); this enum only names
the states.

FinancingTabCounts.title: FinancingTabCounts
FinancingTabCounts.description: The counts the detail page's tab bar shows.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email address of the account to reset

GeneratedDocumentListResponse.title: GeneratedDocumentListResponse
GeneratedDocumentListResponse.description:
The case's produced documents, plus which types can no longer be produced.

``locked_type_codes`` carries the step-18 freeze (R4) so the UI can disable the action instead
of re-deriving a server rule from the financing's returned values. It is keyed by TYPE, not by
produced row: a frozen type is refused whether or not one was ever produced.

GeneratedDocumentRow.title: GeneratedDocumentRow
GeneratedDocumentRow.description:
One produced document on the case's generated tab (PRD1042-1940, US 1.24). Shows its type, its
file name, when it was produced and by whom. The rendered file is fetched via the media endpoint
(``GET /api/v1/media/{media_id}``). Produced-at is given in UTC and in the tenant business timezone
(Europe/Berlin, no zone label).

GuarantorAddRequest.title: GuarantorAddRequest
GuarantorAddRequest.description:
Add a guarantor to a contract (PRD1042-1923, US 1.7).

Exactly ONE of ``existing_partner_id`` (link a partner already in the register — any status, a
Partner is live from creation) or ``identity`` (create it confirmed). ``kind_of_obligation`` is
OPTIONAL and its value set is not closed (1923-OQ-01) — validated in the service, not pinned to a
hard enum here.

GuarantorLinkResponse.title: GuarantorLinkResponse
GuarantorLinkResponse.description: A guarantor linked to a contract.

GuarantorListItem.title: GuarantorListItem
GuarantorListItem.description: One live guarantor on a contract, for the summary.

GuarantorListResponse.title: GuarantorListResponse
GuarantorListResponse.description: The guarantors a contract carries and how many (PRD1042-1923). Empty is normal, not incomplete.

GuarantorPreviewRequest.title: GuarantorPreviewRequest
GuarantorPreviewRequest.description: Search the partner register for a guarantor before creating — the identity to match on.

GuarantorRemoveRequest.title: GuarantorRemoveRequest
GuarantorRemoveRequest.description: Soft-remove a guarantor link — the reason is recorded (history preserved).

ImportBatchPreviewResponse.title: ImportBatchPreviewResponse
ImportBatchPreviewResponse.description: The staged run: summary counts + the rows (paged).

ImportBatchResponse.title: ImportBatchResponse
ImportBatchResponse.description:
The result screen of an upload (PRD1042-1921): how many rows the file held, how many are valid and
how many failed — the user carries on with the valid rows without waiting for the rest. There is
deliberately NO duplicate count (repeat detection is undecided, 1920-OQ-02). A FAILED batch carries
the per-file precondition finding naming which company is affected and what it is missing.

ImportCommitResponse.title: ImportCommitResponse
ImportCommitResponse.description: The commit outcome: how many rows became contracts; the rest stay for the correction file.

ImportRowItem.title: ImportRowItem
ImportRowItem.description:
One staged row of an import run (PRD1042-1921, US 1.5).

A rejected row names the line, the field and the reason in language the uploader can act on, and its
kind: ``correctable`` comes back editable in the correction file; ``factual`` comes back with the
reason and no editable column.

ImportRowStatus.title: ImportRowStatus
ImportRowStatus.description:
The state of one staged row (PRD1042-1921, US 1.5).

A row that does not pass is not imported at all — partial import is the normal case. ``VALID`` rows
become ``COMMITTED`` when the batch commits; ``REJECTED`` rows come back in the correction file and
are re-uploaded as a NEW run (matched on the leasing company's contract number within the request, so
a re-upload never duplicates).

IndustryClassResponse.title: IndustryClassResponse
IndustryClassResponse.description: One WZ 2008 subclass: the code that is stored, and its wording in both languages.

InheritedGDValues.title: InheritedGDValues
InheritedGDValues.description:
Global Default parent values shown alongside a PS override/deactivate row.

Read-only display derived from the inheritance model (US 15.4). Inherited (immutable)
attributes and the overridable attributes are both surfaced so the UI can render the
Global Default value next to the override value.

InstalmentFrequency.title: InstalmentFrequency
InstalmentFrequency.description:
How often the instalment falls due (PRD1042-1925, US 1.9) — CANONICAL definition.

Captured on the contract; the platform never assumes monthly (never defaulted). Only the monthly
case is calibrated for the calculation (30/360, arrears) — a non-monthly contract can be CAPTURED,
but must not run silently through the monthly-only model (PRD1042-1925 R4); the calculation support
for the other cadences is deferred. ``financing/domain/enums.py`` imports this enum rather than
redeclaring it (one source of truth).

access_valid_until.description: Auditor only — end of access window
