lc_partner_id.description: Required for leasing_company_user; must be null for all other roles

KeepBothRequest.title: KeepBothRequest
KeepBothRequest.description: Keep both records — the pair is two different parties (US-1.99). The note is optional.

LCObligationFile.title: LCObligationFile
LCObligationFile.description:
BUG-159 — one file filed against an obligation, as the leasing company sees it. No document id,
no review metadata beyond the bank's reason for an invalid file, and an uploader that is only ever
the company itself or "the bank" — never a bank role.

LcCaseDetailResponse.title: LcCaseDetailResponse
LcCaseDetailResponse.description:
A leasing company's restricted view of one of its own cases (US 1.35 / PRD1042-1951).

The same record the bank sees, through a narrower window: only what the leasing company may see.
`display_status` is derived (never stored) and, since US-1.92, never from the financing: it is the
request's status (Cancelled when cancelled), preserving the MISSING_INFORMATION vs REWORK
distinction (their external labels are a display question, 1951-OQ-02). The financing state is
bank-only (Milestone 1 Rule 01 R1, Rule 02 §2.3 A), so no field names it and there is no
`primary_entity`. `case_status` (US 1.49) is the case's own lifecycle label (open / waiting / done /
cancelled), non-sensitive. US-1.92 adds `request_status`
(Milestone 1 Rule 06 §1.2 shows "Request <status>" to the LC, and its status badge is the request
status only, Rule 02 P1) and `started_by_lc_name` ("Started by <LC name>" on a portal case). The
bounded field set is still the access control: bank-internal fields remain absent by construction
and cannot leak — no `owner_user_id`, no `product_template_id` / `framework_agreement_id`, no
routing exception or decision round, no financing state or figures (rate / loan number / loan
account), no checklist, no calculation, no pricing.
Enforced at query level (company + tenant scope), never by hiding in the UI. There is deliberately
no bank-side counterpart to this schema — it is not a copy of `CaseResponse` with fields removed,
it is its own least-privilege projection.

LcCaseListItem.title: LcCaseListItem
LcCaseListItem.description:
One row of a leasing company's own case list (US 1.35 / PRD1042-1951).

**Deliberately not `CaseListItem`.** Until 2026-09-11 `GET /lc/cases` answered with the bank's
own list model — described in the route as "a thin, clearly-named alias" — which handed a
leasing-company user `owner_user_id`, `created_by`, `decision_round`, `request_status`,
`routing_exception` and `origin_financing_id`. `decision_round` alone states how many times the
bank returned the request, which is the "internal review notes" the story withholds by name.
The detail projection had always been least-privilege; only the list was aliased. The field set
here is the access control, exactly as in `LcCaseDetailResponse`: bank-internal fields are
absent by construction and cannot be leaked by a future serializer change.

Same fields as the detail projection. They are kept as two models rather than one alias because
a list and a detail diverge on their own schedules, and the next field added to one must be a
decision about the other rather than an accident.

LcCaseListResponse.title: LcCaseListResponse
LcCaseListResponse.description:
The leasing company's own case list.

No `counts_by_status`: that facet is the bank work list's queue instrument, grouped over stored
bank columns, and no portal surface consumes it. Leaving it out keeps the projection to what the
portal actually shows.

LcCaseReviewResponse.title: LcCaseReviewResponse
LcCaseReviewResponse.description:
The leasing company's review of its own request (BUG-072, ``GET /lc/cases/{id}/review``).

The bank's review with the leasing company's projection as the case block and no financing block — the
bank-internal fields are absent from the model, so no serializer change can re-expose them (Rule 01 §3).
The product template is bank configuration and is left out too.

LcCommentNotificationItem.title: LcCommentNotificationItem
LcCommentNotificationItem.description:
US-1.113 (AC1) — one bell entry: a case on which the bank left the leasing-company user a
comment it has not marked as seen. Rendered "<author> commented on <case>" · "Visible to the
leasing company · <time>", and it leads to the case.

LcFileUploader.title: LcFileUploader
LcFileUploader.description:
BUG-159 — who filed a document, as a leasing company may be told it: itself, or the bank. Which
bank role uploaded is bank-internal (PRD1042-1796 item 9), so there is no finer value.

LcFinancingAgreementOption.title: LcFinancingAgreementOption
LcFinancingAgreementOption.description: P30-32 — one framework agreement the leasing company's listed financings name (the filter).

LcFinancingListItem.title: LcFinancingListItem
LcFinancingListItem.description:
One row of the leasing company's own financings (P29-14, P30-32) — the portal's projection.

Deliberately narrow: the status only in the portal's own wording (``portal_status``, Q-118 — never
the financing's status code), no product template (bank-internal, rule 03 D3, Q-100 open), no rate,
loan or case-internal fields. The model is the guard — a field absent here cannot be re-exposed by
a serializer change.

LcPortalSummaryResponse.title: LcPortalSummaryResponse
LcPortalSummaryResponse.description:
The leasing company's dashboard figures over ALL of its own cases (BUG-145).

Counted server-side from one grouped query, so the figures do not depend on how many cases the
portal happened to load. Each case counts under the status badge the portal list shows it with
(the request's own status; the financing is never shown to the leasing company).

LcWithdrawalNoticeRequest.title: LcWithdrawalNoticeRequest
LcWithdrawalNoticeRequest.description:
P29-11 — "Tell the bank you are withdrawing": the leasing company's optional message to the bank.

Stored as typed on the case thread when given (the same rule and limit as a comment); blank or
omitted → no comment, only the activity entry.

LeaseCashFlowRead.title: LeaseCashFlowRead
LeaseCashFlowRead.description:
P30-12 — the Overview's Lease cash flow card (M2 spec §4.5). ``unavailable`` names why there is
nothing to show (no_financing · no_value_date · no_quota · no_lease_plan); every figure is then null
and ``rows`` empty.

LeaseCashFlowRowRead.title: LeaseCashFlowRowRead
LeaseCashFlowRowRead.description: P30-12 — one lease payment of the contract over the financing period.

LeaseCashFlowUnavailable.title: LeaseCashFlowUnavailable
LeaseCashFlowUnavailable.description: Why the card has no cash flow to show (wire values; the client labels them).

LeaseObjectCreate.title: LeaseObjectCreate
LeaseObjectCreate.description:
Fields accepted when adding a lease object to a contract.

BUG-156: the net acquisition cost is required on every object (the client's rule), so a create
without it is a 422 like any missing required field. The MILK import writes through the service,
not this schema; a cost-less object from any source is caught by the submit check.

LeaseObjectEdit.title: LeaseObjectEdit
LeaseObjectEdit.description:
Fields accepted when editing a lease object (partial, ``model_fields_set``).

BUG-156: leaving ``acquisition_cost`` out keeps the stored value (an object saved before the rule
keeps none until it is entered); sending it as ``null`` would clear a required field and is a 422.

LeaseObjectRead.title: LeaseObjectRead
LeaseObjectRead.description:
A lease object plus its advisory signals (PRD1042-1924, US 1.8).

``residual_warning`` is the quittable residual > acquisition-cost message (null when fine — never a
refusal). The acquisition cost is returned as entered — there is no per-vehicle cap (P30-52, Q-132:
the 300,000 is applied outside RefiNext). ``missing_for_vehicle`` lists the vehicle-conditional fields still
absent (ZLB II / DAT) — a completeness signal, not a save block. ``missing_fields`` lists every
mandatory field still empty (US-1.83): description, group, ZLB II for a vehicle, acquisition cost —
completeness on an existing object, never a save block (rule 04 O4).

LeaseObjectRemove.title: LeaseObjectRemove
LeaseObjectRemove.description: The reason a lease object is removed — preserved with the soft-removed record.

LeasingCompanyResolutionResponse.title: LeasingCompanyResolutionResponse
LeasingCompanyResolutionResponse.description:
Wizard step 1 before the case exists (Milestone 1 rule 03 §2.3, US-1.78): what the chosen
company resolves to. The framework agreement is the one in force today, and the bank product
template is the one it sets; neither is a choice, so neither has a picker.

``agreement_id`` null = no agreement in force ("No active framework agreement for this leasing
company."); ``has_usable_template`` false = the agreement sets no usable template. Either way the
step cannot continue. For a leasing-company user (``bank_side_visible`` false) the quota, the
framework volume and the template are always null — it reads only *whether* a usable template
resolves (BUG-114), never which; it does read its own agreement's fee and accounts, as the
prototype shows them.

LesseeCaptureRequest.title: LesseeCaptureRequest
LesseeCaptureRequest.description:
Capture the lessee on a contract (PRD1042-1922, US 1.6). Exactly ONE of ``existing_partner_id``
(link a partner already in the register) or ``identity`` (create it confirmed) must be given.
A party created here also takes the party mask's addresses and dealer numbers
(``NewPartyExtras``, P30-17).

LesseeLinkResponse.title: LesseeLinkResponse
LesseeLinkResponse.description: The lessee linked to the contract.

LesseePreviewRequest.title: LesseePreviewRequest
LesseePreviewRequest.description: Search the partner register for the lessee before creating — the identity to match on.

LesseeUnlinkResponse.title: LesseeUnlinkResponse
LesseeUnlinkResponse.description:
The contract after its lessee is unlinked (PRD1042-2165) — the reference is now null. The
partner itself stays in the registry; only this contract's lessee slot is cleared.

LoanPaymentPlanRead.title: LoanPaymentPlanRead
LoanPaymentPlanRead.description:
P30-10 — the contract's Loan payment plan tab: the repayment schedule of its own financing (a package's
whole schedule), read-only. ``unavailable`` names why there is nothing to show (no_financing ·
not_calculated · not_available — the last for a leasing-company caller instead of not_calculated); every
other field is then null and ``rows`` empty. The bank reads the schedule adjusted for settled redemptions
(``adjusted_for_redemptions``); a leasing-company caller reads the plan as priced and gets ``bank = null``.

LoanPaymentPlanUnavailable.title: LoanPaymentPlanUnavailable
LoanPaymentPlanUnavailable.description:
P30-10 — why the contract's Loan payment plan tab has no schedule to show.

Wire values; the client labels them. A leasing-company caller never gets ``not_calculated``: the portal is told only that the
plan is ``not_available`` yet, never why (the calculation is the bank's working state).

LoanPlanBankDetailsRead.title: LoanPlanBankDetailsRead
LoanPlanBankDetailsRead.description: P30-10 — bank-only details next to the plan; the whole object is null for a leasing-company caller.

LoanPlanFinancingRead.title: LoanPlanFinancingRead
LoanPlanFinancingRead.description: P30-10 — the financing whose schedule the tab shows.

next_step.title: Next Step
next_step.description: otp — send OTP code to /auth/otp/verify; mfa — send TOTP code to /auth/mfa/verify; mfa_setup — no MFA yet, enroll at /auth/mfa/enroll; session — auth cookies already set (MFA freshness bypass), redirect to dashboard

token.title: Token
token.description: Short-lived token (5 min) for the next step. Null when next_step=session.

expires_in.title: Expires In
expires_in.description: Seconds until token expires. Null when next_step=session.

ManualPlanRowRequest.title: ManualPlanRowRequest
ManualPlanRowRequest.description:
One hand-entered row. ``row_type`` replaced the old ``is_final`` boolean — finality is now
derived from the type in the database, so a caller says what the row IS.

MarkNonPerforming.title: MarkNonPerforming
MarkNonPerforming.description:
P30-14 — "Mark as non-performing": an optional reason, kept with the audit entry (approved
prototype ``mark-np``: "Reason — Optional").

MarketValueIndicator.title: MarketValueIndicator
MarketValueIndicator.description:
The market-value indicator on an object (PRD1042-1924).

Carries ``i.O.`` — the ONLY confirmed value. This is **not** a "valuation performed" flag: the
earlier candidate field for that was withdrawn (no such indicator exists). It states that the
recorded market value is in order, a different statement from "a valuation was done".

MeasurementBasis.title: MeasurementBasis
MeasurementBasis.description:
How a refinancing's disbursement is measured (PRD1042-11, US 1.39, §6.5.1).

A property of the bank product template, one per leasing company (D-129) — never a per-deal mode and
never inferred from the repayment profile. Member ``SCREAMING_SNAKE``, value lowercase, matching the
``RefusalReason`` / ``FinancingKind`` idiom.

MergeDocumentsRequest.title: MergeDocumentsRequest
MergeDocumentsRequest.description: The documents to merge. An empty pick is answered 422 ``DOCUMENT_MERGE_NOTHING_SELECTED``.

MergeDuplicateRequest.title: MergeDuplicateRequest
MergeDuplicateRequest.description:
Merge the pair in the chosen direction (US-1.99): ``survivor_partner_id`` stays, the other
record is retired and its references move to the survivor. No reason code (P30-25, client round 2
point 3) — the optional note records a reason where there is one.

MergeSourceResponse.title: MergeSourceResponse
MergeSourceResponse.description: One document the merge modal may offer (US-1.110, rule 06 §5.5).

code.title: Code
code.description: First TOTP code from authenticator app

recovery_codes.title: Recovery Codes
recovery_codes.description: 10 single-use recovery codes — show once, save immediately

qr_code.title: Qr Code
qr_code.description: Base64-encoded PNG QR code for scanning in authenticator app

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Manual entry key (for users who can't scan QR)

mfa_required.title: Mfa Required
mfa_required.description: Set to true to require MFA for all tenant-level users

code.title: Code
code.description: 6-digit TOTP code or 20-char hex recovery code

new_recovery_codes.title: New Recovery Codes
new_recovery_codes.description: New recovery codes — present only when a recovery code was used. Show to user immediately.

MilkContractItem.title: MilkContractItem
MilkContractItem.description:
One contract the delivery carries, for the screen shown when a file is accepted.

What the row says, not what would be written: the submitter sees the package they are about to
hand over. ``object_count`` follows the object-list rule — the list where a contract has one,
otherwise the single object on its own row.

MilkFindingItem.title: MilkFindingItem
MilkFindingItem.description: One thing wrong with the delivery.

MilkImportResponse.title: MilkImportResponse
MilkImportResponse.description:
What one committed MILK delivery produced.

Reports what was WRITTEN, not what the file held — the two differ on purpose and the difference
is the point. ``objects_created`` follows the object-list rule, so a contract with a list
contributes its listed objects and not the summary on its own row.

``collaterals_created`` counts the seven party-less collateral types. ``GUARANTEE`` rows are
counted apart, in ``guarantees_not_written``, because they cannot be written yet — not because
they were not delivered. No payment plans are reported because none are written.

MilkValidationResponse.title: MilkValidationResponse
MilkValidationResponse.description:
The answer for one delivery — decided at FILE level.

``accepted`` is the whole outcome: one error anywhere refuses the file, **including the rows that
passed** (§5). There is deliberately no per-row acceptance and no success list, because nothing
is partially imported and a success report would have no subject.

``accepted: true`` does **not** mean anything was imported. Import is a separate step and is not
built: it is blocked on the party decision (Q-079) and on twelve columns with no field to land in
(BUG-059). This endpoint answers whether the file *would* be acceptable.

MiscDocumentResponse.title: MiscDocumentResponse
MiscDocumentResponse.description: PRD1042-2263 — one free-form document in a case's Miscellaneous section.

pending_approval_note.title: Pending Approval Note
pending_approval_note.default: Module activation is pending a second System Admin's approval (POST /governed-actions/{id}/approve). The module stays in 'pending_enforcement' and its routes answer 404 until approved. Track pending approvals at GET /governed-actions?status=pending.

ModuleActivationResponse.title: ModuleActivationResponse
ModuleActivationResponse.description:
BUG-015 — the 201 body of a module-activation request.

Activation is a Four-Eyes governed action: the module is set to `pending_enforcement` and a SECOND
System Admin must approve before it becomes `active`. Until then every route the module gates
answers a generic 404 (existence non-disclosure, by design). The bare `GovernedActionResponse`
carried nothing about the module's new state, so an admin read "201 Created" as "the module is now
usable" and was surprised by the downstream 404. This response makes the state explicit — the
governed action PLUS the module's `pending_enforcement` status and where to track the approval.

NewOrUsed.title: NewOrUsed
NewOrUsed.description:
Whether the object is new or used (PRD1042-1924).

A separate attribute — never folded into the object group or sub-group. Defaults to ``NEW`` at
capture. No valuation rule is keyed to it (the spec builds no such rule).

ObjectClassificationResponse.title: ObjectClassificationResponse
ObjectClassificationResponse.description: The object classification config (groups + sub-groups + fahrzeug flag) — for the FE picker.

ObjectGroupItem.title: ObjectGroupItem
ObjectGroupItem.description:
One classification group from the config file — with its is-vehicle flag and its sub-groups
(the fuel set for vehicle groups).

ObjectLocation.title: ObjectLocation
ObjectLocation.description:
Whether the object is located in Germany or abroad (PRD1042-2269) — MILK ``Standort Inl./Ausl.``.

Two values because that is what the file carries; the discussion that also raised picking the
country is not settled, so no country is inferred from this. Separate from the free-text
``location_and_region``, which it does not replace.

OsPlusEditRequest.title: OsPlusEditRequest
OsPlusEditRequest.description:
P30-50 — the OS+ person number on its own, for the Power User, who has no Edit party (P30-18).
``version`` is the one the page loaded; ``null`` clears the number.

PackageTotalsRead.title: PackageTotalsRead
PackageTotalsRead.description:
DISPLAY sums for a request's contract set (PRD1042-1928) — NEVER a calculation input.

``residual_sum`` is the sum of the active contracts' residuals, shown so the user sees the package
size. ``acquisition_cost_sum`` / ``special_payment_sum`` are object-level (US-1.8) and are ``null``
until the object model exists. The package schedule calculation (1928-R7) is deliberately not built.

total.title: Total
total.description: Total number of users matching current filters

PairSideRoleResponse.title: PairSideRoleResponse
PairSideRoleResponse.description: A role the record plays: ``lessee`` / ``guarantor`` / ``collateral_guarantor`` on a request.

PartnerAddressInput.title: PartnerAddressInput
PartnerAddressInput.description:
One address as submitted. `label` is what the list shows ("Registered office").

Write-side mandatory fields match `RegisteredAddressInput` so the two capture paths agree;
`house_number` and `address_line_2` are the click dummy's additions and are optional because a
German address line is frequently "Landsberger Straße 212" with the number already in it.

PartnerCaptureRequest.title: PartnerCaptureRequest
PartnerCaptureRequest.description:
Create a party from the partner register's New party (P30-17) — the same party mask as the
contract form's Create party, and the same outcome: the party is created **confirmed** with its
addresses and dealer numbers in one transaction. An exact match to a confirmed
partner is returned as it is (nothing typed is written onto it), unless ``keep_both``: the bank
user's Keep both in the Matching candidates dialog, which creates the typed party and leaves the
pair for the bank. ``duplicate_note`` is stored on the pair a Keep both opens.

PartnerCaptureResponse.title: PartnerCaptureResponse
PartnerCaptureResponse.description: The party the capture resolved to — created confirmed (201) or the existing one (200).

PartnerConnectionItem.title: PartnerConnectionItem
PartnerConnectionItem.description:
One place this party already appears — a contract it is on, or the request that carries it.

The read model behind the Create-partner modal's Connections tab: before creating a party a
clerk needs to see where an existing one is already engaged, in which role, for whom, and in
what state. It is a projection over existing links (``Contract.lessee_partner_id`` and
``ContractGuarantor``), never a new carrier — nothing here is stored.

``status`` is the CASE display status (``cases/domain/status.py::derive_display_status``), for
contracts too, and that is deliberate: the state a user reads off a contract ("draft",
"committed") is the state of the deal it rides in, while ``Contract.contract_status`` only
distinguishes active from cancelled. A cancelled contract overrides its case's value — a
cancelled row must never read as live.

PartnerDocumentItem.title: PartnerDocumentItem
PartnerDocumentItem.description:
One row of the Documents read.

``media_object_id`` is what the interface's "Open" streams (``GET /media/{id}``) — the id is
handed out rather than a URL, because the file is never public and every read goes through that
endpoint's authorization (``media/application/access.py``).

``document_type_name`` is resolved from the tenant's document-type registry so the table can
show what the registry calls the type today; ``document_type_code`` is the stable identity other
modules resolve against. Both travel: the name for the eye, the code for anything mechanical.

PartnerRelationshipCreateRequest.title: PartnerRelationshipCreateRequest
PartnerRelationshipCreateRequest.description:
One directional edge, as the Relationships tab captures it.

``direction`` is what the interface's "Swap direction" toggles, and it is the whole reason the
pair is not symmetric: ``outgoing`` means *this party is the `<type>` of the other*, ``incoming``
means *the other is the `<type>` of this party*. The service turns it into which id goes in
which column, so the client never has to know the storage shape.

PartnerRelationshipItem.title: PartnerRelationshipItem
PartnerRelationshipItem.description:
One row of the Relationships read, told from the asking party's point of view.

The written-out sentence ("X is the parent of this party") is composed by the CLIENT from
``relationship_type`` + ``direction``, never here: it is UI copy and has to exist in both
locales, and this API ships no localized strings.

``is_editable`` is false for the ``beneficial_owner`` rows projected from ``partner_ubo_ownership``
— they are shown so the table is the whole picture, but they are maintained where their rules
live, not on this surface.

PartnerRelationshipType.title: PartnerRelationshipType
PartnerRelationshipType.description:
How one party stands to another — the Create-partner modal's Relationships tab.

A relationship is DIRECTIONAL: the row reads *from* **is the <type> of** *to*, which is what the
interface's "Swap direction" writes. Storing the direction rather than a pair of mirrored rows
keeps one fact in one place — "A is the parent of B" and "B is a subsidiary of A" are the same
edge read from two ends, and materialising both would let them drift apart.

**`BENEFICIAL_OWNER` is deliberately absent**, although the prototype's picker offers it. That
fact already has a carrier with rules of its own — :class:`UboOwnershipRecord`: the owner must be
a CONFIRMED legal entity, the target a CONFIRMED natural person, the shares must total no more
than 100%, and the set drives ``ubo_completeness_status``. A second table accepting the same fact
under looser rules is exactly the drift this module refuses elsewhere, and a party being created
is DRAFT — so a beneficial-owner row captured there could never satisfy those rules anyway. The
read path still RETURNS a ``beneficial_owner`` row type, projected from the UBO records and
marked not editable, so the tab shows the whole picture out of one carrier per fact.

PartyAddressUpdate.title: PartyAddressUpdate
PartyAddressUpdate.description: An address the edit changes, named by its id.

PartyDuplicateState.title: PartyDuplicateState
PartyDuplicateState.description:
A party's duplicate state as its page header shows it (P30-19; M2 spec §6.2): Duplicate pending,
Merged, Kept apart, or none at all.

PartyEditRequest.title: PartyEditRequest
PartyEditRequest.description:
Edit party (P30-18; M2 spec §6.3) — one save for the whole partner page's edit mode: "Nothing is
stored until you save". The identity carries the party's own type (it is never changed); the dealer
numbers are the complete list the party keeps; the address lists are what the edit added, changed
and retired. ``version`` is the one the page loaded: a stale one is refused and nothing is written.
Bank accounts are not edited here — they are maintained on the partner page's Bank accounts tab
(P30-47).

PartyMatchItem.title: PartyMatchItem
PartyMatchItem.description:
One party on the case with its computed match outcome (PRD1042-1929, US 1.13).

Carries the outcome, the partner's status and display name, and ``has_unresolved_duplicate`` — the
advisory duplicate flag (US-1.86) — never the bank's other partner records (candidate ids are not
exposed on the case surface; the resolve/merge screens carry those).

PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod
PaymentMethod.description:
How the lessee pays the instalment (PRD1042-2269) — MILK ``Zahlart``, one value per MILK value.

Named after what MILK delivers rather than after the click dummy's "Direct debit / Transfer",
because the dummy's mapping of ``Selbstzahler`` was never stated (specification open point 8)
and a 1:1 set loses nothing. Captured only: nothing in the calculation reads it.

PaymentMode.title: PaymentMode

PaymentPlanEntryResponse.title: PaymentPlanEntryResponse
PaymentPlanEntryResponse.description:
One entry of a contract's payment plan — date + amount, typed, the residual marked final.

``period`` is the row's 1-based position in the plan and is DERIVED at read time, never stored:
a plan is always replaced wholesale, so the ordinal follows from the stored order and a column
would only be a second carrier of it that can go stale.

``is_final`` is likewise derived — a generated column over ``row_type`` — and stays on the wire
because existing readers use it.

PaymentPlanResponse.title: PaymentPlanResponse
PaymentPlanResponse.description:
A contract's plan, and its component when the case has a financing.

``component`` is **null before the case is committed** — the plan is captured during intake, and
the financing (and therefore the component) is minted only at commit.

PaymentPlanRowType.title: PaymentPlanRowType
PaymentPlanRowType.description:
What one row of a payment plan represents (the prototype's "Type" column).

The click dummy shows three kinds — a down payment, the repeated instalments, and a final
payment — as hardcoded display text on an inert table, so this SET IS OURS, not the client's:
it is the smallest vocabulary that renders that table honestly. Extending an output enum later
is non-breaking (``api-versioning.md`` §3.2); shrinking one is not, which is why it starts at
three rather than guessing at more. **Open with CrossLease** — confirm the vocabulary before it
reaches a report.

``INSTALMENT`` keeps the British spelling used everywhere else in this codebase
(``InstalmentFrequency``, ``instalment_amount``). The prototype's "Installment" is a typo in a
demo array, and matching it would be exactly the cross-layer casing mismatch
``enums-and-constants.md`` exists to prevent.

PendingApprovalResponse.title: PendingApprovalResponse
PendingApprovalResponse.description:
A move that waits for a second person (44-step matrix governance, BUG-098 / BUG-099): nothing
changed yet; a different Back Office user approves the governed action in Pending approvals.

PerformanceStatus.title: PerformanceStatus
PerformanceStatus.description:
P30-14 — the contract's performance status (M2 spec §4.1), a fact separate from its refinancing
status. ``PERFORMING`` by default; ``NON_PERFORMING`` is a manual marker set by Front or Back Office
on a Financed contract — never derived from the number of direct debit returns. Whether it can be set
back to performing is open (spec §9 #9), so no transition out of it exists.

PhaseProgressResponse.title: PhaseProgressResponse
PhaseProgressResponse.description: One phase's progress (US-1.18 / PRD1042-1934). `phase_name` is None for the unphased bucket.

PlanCoverageResponse.title: PlanCoverageResponse
PlanCoverageResponse.description:
Whether the plan's instalment rows span the whole term (US-1.117, rule 04 §6.4) — a warning,
never a block. ``covered_months`` counts calendar months from the first instalment's due date to
the last, inclusive.

PortalDocumentTypeItem.title: PortalDocumentTypeItem
PortalDocumentTypeItem.description: A document type the portal may upload a party document under (P30-31) — code and name only.

PortalFinancingStatus.title: PortalFinancingStatus
PortalFinancingStatus.description:
P30-32 — the financing status in the leasing company's wording (approved prototype 30 Sep,
``PORTAL_FIN_STATUS``; Q-118). Declared in lifecycle order — the order the portal's Status column
sorts in. Mapped from the financing's own status by ``portal_financing_status``; a financing whose
status has no portal value (Draft, Run-out, …) is not listed at all.

RecordDeviationRequest.title: RecordDeviationRequest
RecordDeviationRequest.description:
Record a hand-compared document-vs-request deviation (PRD1042-1938, US 1.22). The platform never
reads the value out of the document — the user types what they compared.

RecordLoanValuesRequest.title: RecordLoanValuesRequest
RecordLoanValuesRequest.description:
Record the core-system returned values on the financing (PRD1042-1941, US 1.25).

Both are recorded together (one lifecycle). Either may be null — e.g. the loan number is linked to
an already-registered loan while the account is still pending — but the request always carries both
slots, so a value is never silently left at its previous state.

value_date.title: Value Date
value_date.description: The date the redemption is effective from

RedemptionCaptureRequest.title: RedemptionCaptureRequest
RedemptionCaptureRequest.description:
What is owed to redeem the contract set, and from when.

``amount`` is a STATED figure, not a computed one — the calculation engine's redemption values
are deferred, and this is the number the bank works out today. Positive: a redemption of zero or
less is not a correction, it is a mistake.

RedemptionListItem.title: RedemptionListItem
RedemptionListItem.description:
One row of the parent case's Redemption tab.

``kind`` is the case type (single vs package) — derived from how many contracts are affected,
never declared. ``contract_numbers`` names those contracts by the leasing company's own number,
which is what a person recognises. Every figure is nullable: a redemption case exists from the
moment it is started, before anyone has worked out what it is worth.

RedemptionResponse.title: RedemptionResponse
RedemptionResponse.description:
One redemption's figures. ``status`` is ``pending`` until the money lands, then ``settled``
(terminal — only the settle endpoint moves it).

RedemptionStatus.title: RedemptionStatus
RedemptionStatus.description:
Where a redemption stands (US 1.37 follow-up cases, Milestone-1 Redemption tab).

A redemption is a contract set being paid off early. Two values, because that is what the
process distinguishes: the figure has been agreed and is owed (``PENDING``), or the money has
arrived and the redemption is closed (``SETTLED``).

Deliberately NOT a third "cancelled" value: a redemption that does not happen is a cancelled
CASE (``CaseStatus.CANCELLED`` on the follow-up case), not a settled-and-reversed redemption —
the case carries the cancellation, this field carries the money.

``SETTLED`` is terminal. It is reached only through the guarded transition in
``CaseService.settle_redemption``, never by writing the column.

RedetermineCollateralRequest.title: RedetermineCollateralRequest
RedetermineCollateralRequest.description:
Propose a re-determined package collateral total (P29-06). It becomes a version only when a
second Back Office person approves it.

RefiLoanValueDateRule.title: RefiLoanValueDateRule
RefiLoanValueDateRule.description:
PRD1042-1799 CR-FA-01 (10 Aug 2026) — the Refi Loan Value Date (Valuta Refi-Darlehen) is a
*value-date rule*, not a currency. Confirmed values: ``first_of_month`` ("zum 01. des Monats",
5 of 7 leasing companies) and ``variable`` ("variabel", 1).

RefinancingForm.title: RefinancingForm
RefinancingForm.description:
CR-BPT-08 item 7: how the bank's own refinancing loan is repaid. The single §3 box
(replaces the former 6-value FinancingType and the redundant CalculationModel).

RegisteredAddress.title: RegisteredAddress
RegisteredAddress.description: Address as returned in responses. Lenient — legacy rows may be incomplete.

RegisteredAddressInput.title: RegisteredAddressInput
RegisteredAddressInput.description: Address as submitted by a client. All fields mandatory except state_region.

RegistrationPartTwoStatus.title: RegistrationPartTwoStatus
RegistrationPartTwoStatus.description: Vehicle registration part II (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II) — vehicles only (Philipp).

RegistryRole.title: RegistryRole
RegistryRole.description:
The registry's Role filter — read off the data, never assigned (spec §6.1: "All / Leasing company /
Lessee / Guarantor / Supplier — read off the data").

* leasing company — holds a dealer number, or is the leasing company of a framework agreement
* lessee — the lessee of a live contract
* guarantor — a guarantor, or the guarantor of a guarantee collateral, on a live contract
* supplier — no party is linked as a supplier yet (a lease object names its supplier as text), so
  the filter finds nobody; spec §9 records the same of the test data.

RejectDocumentRequest.title: RejectDocumentRequest
RejectDocumentRequest.description:
Reject one filed document on a case (US-1.109, rule 06 DC7). The reason is mandatory: it is
shown in red under the file and recorded in the case's Activity trail. 1–255 characters (the
limit is our choice, not a source rule).

RepaymentRead.title: RepaymentRead
RepaymentRead.description: The repayment schedule and the figures read off it (P29-04). Absent before ReadyForSetup.

RepaymentRowRead.title: RepaymentRowRead
RepaymentRowRead.description:
One row of the repayment schedule (P29-04): the payout, then the instalments — and, from P29-17,
a settled redemption on its value date.

RequestStatus.title: RequestStatus
RequestStatus.description:
The refinancing request's state.

`MISSING_INFORMATION` and `REWORK` are separate values and must not be merged: the first is a
question back to the submitter, the second is a structured correction loop. `COMMITTED` is a
status of the request and never of the financing (PRD1042-1918).

token.title: Token
token.description: Password reset token from the email link

password.title: Password
password.description: Min 8 chars, at least 1 uppercase and 1 number

mfa_required.title: Mfa Required
mfa_required.description: True when user's role requires MFA — FE must call POST /auth/password/reset/verify

mfa_token.title: Mfa Token
mfa_token.description: Short-lived token (5 min) to pass to /auth/password/reset/verify. Present only when mfa_required=True.

code.title: Code
code.description: 6-digit TOTP code or 20-char hex recovery code

new_recovery_codes.title: New Recovery Codes
new_recovery_codes.description: New recovery codes — present only when a recovery code was used. Show to user immediately.

ReviewContractItem.title: ReviewContractItem
ReviewContractItem.description:
One contract row on the review summary — the identifying facts + its completeness badge, not the
full contract record (the summary has a way back into the capture screen for the rest).

ReviewFinancingSummary.title: ReviewFinancingSummary
ReviewFinancingSummary.description:
The financing figures on the review. The rate/quota/value-date carriers are shown; the financing
VOLUME is the payout amount (PRD1042-1931's financing amount) and is DERIVED — it is reported as
``pending`` until the calculation is built (US-1.11 + 1931-OQ-03), never a computed or assumed
value.

RunOutRequest.title: RunOutRequest
RunOutRequest.description: Why the disbursed financing runs out (F-6) — kept on the governed action and in the audit.

ScheduleLineResponse.title: ScheduleLineResponse
ScheduleLineResponse.description: One amortisation-schedule line (§6.5.3). ``payment == interest + principal`` on every line.

SetCollateralTotalRequest.title: SetCollateralTotalRequest
SetCollateralTotalRequest.description:
Record the FIRST package collateral total — version 1, saved directly (P29-06); later changes
are re-determinations. Stored as entered — no cap (P30-44; Q-132).

SetCollateralTypeRequest.title: SetCollateralTypeRequest
SetCollateralTypeRequest.description: Set the kind of security backing the package (US 1.14 / PRD1042-1930). Single selection.

SetManualPlanRequest.title: SetManualPlanRequest
SetManualPlanRequest.description:
Replace a contract's plan with hand-entered rows (the catch-all for irregular structures).

A MANUAL plan is never regenerated from terms (R2). At most one row is the final (residual) entry.

token.title: Token
token.description: Invitation token from the activation email link

password.title: Password
password.description: Min 8 chars, at least 1 uppercase and 1 number

mfa_enrollment_required.title: Mfa Enrollment Required
mfa_enrollment_required.description: True when the user's role/tenant requires MFA — FE must redirect to /auth/mfa/enroll

mfa_token.title: Mfa Token
mfa_token.description: Short-lived setup token to pass to /auth/mfa/enroll (present only when mfa_enrollment_required=True)

StartCaseRequest.title: StartCaseRequest
StartCaseRequest.description:
Starting a case asks for the case type first.

A refinancing request opens the guided wizard; the other six do not — each has its own entry
surface. That is a front-end consequence of this field, not a second endpoint.

StateTransitionOutcome.title: StateTransitionOutcome
StateTransitionOutcome.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 5 (AC §5) — permitted outcomes of a state_transition task. Per-task set
(Laurence-confirmed), not a value set of the type. Main process step 4 carries all four; package
redemption step 4's set is seed-only (OP-3, unnamed) and does not affect this schema.

SubmitResultResponse.title: SubmitResultResponse
SubmitResultResponse.description:
The result of submitting a request — the case after the DRAFT → SUBMITTED transition plus the
submission audit (who / when). A failed submission does not reach here: the gate failures come back
as a 422 carrying the typed ``failed_checks`` list.

effective_from.title: Effective From
effective_from.description: Suspension start — omitted/past for immediate on countersignature, future for scheduled

effective_from.title: Effective From
effective_from.description: Suspension start — past/now for immediate, future for scheduled

TaskApplicability.title: TaskApplicability
TaskApplicability.description:
PRD1042-1790 item 4/11 — when a task applies. ``rule`` is evaluated continuously (recorded
with the value read and the rule applied); ``person`` is resolved by a case worker as not
required / not available. Both the continuous evaluation and the person resolution are
case-runtime; this enum is the authoring-side attribute.

TaskResponsibleRole.title: TaskResponsibleRole
TaskResponsibleRole.description:
Legacy single-value responsible role (US 15.x). Retired: new authoring uses the
``responsible_roles`` SET of platform ``UserRole`` values (PRD1042-1892 item 13). Kept only for
reading historical rows.

TaskType.title: TaskType
TaskType.description:
What a task *demands*, distinct from ``TaskCategory`` (a subject-area classification). The type
decides what opens for the worker and how the task closes.

PRD1042-1894 Block 3 (AC §5, Laurence 12 Aug): **SEVEN types**. ``four_eyes_sign_off`` was removed
— four eyes is a **flag on the task** (``four_eyes``) plus its exclusion set, NOT a kind of work
(eleven of the twelve four-eyes steps are a tick by a second person, one is a state transition).

TenantSupportResponse.title: TenantSupportResponse
TenantSupportResponse.description:
Read-only tenant view for Support Users with active grant.

Deliberately limited — governance actors, licence limits, legal hold,
and countersignatory details are excluded per US 29.4 security requirements.

UpdateFinancingDocumentRequest.title: UpdateFinancingDocumentRequest
UpdateFinancingDocumentRequest.description:
Set or clear a financing document's type and label. Both optional — the prototype's picker
starts unset ("Select") and the label is optional.

UpdateMaintainedValuesRequest.title: UpdateMaintainedValuesRequest
UpdateMaintainedValuesRequest.description:
P29-03 — edit the hand-maintained values on the financing's Data tab.

Partial: only the fields sent change; a field sent as null is cleared ("not recorded", never
zero). At least one field is required. The loan number and account are editable from SetUp
onwards (409 ``FINANCING_VALUES_LOCKED`` before); Sollbelastung and Habenausgleich always.

UpdateMiscDocumentRequest.title: UpdateMiscDocumentRequest
UpdateMiscDocumentRequest.description:
Set/clear the document type + optional label on a miscellaneous document. Both nullable — the
prototype's picker starts at 'Select' (unset) and the label is optional.

UpdateTermsRequest.title: UpdateTermsRequest
UpdateTermsRequest.description:
Save every term of the Calculations tab in one write (PRD1042-2266, Rule 07 §3, §9).

A full replacement (``PUT``): every field is sent, ``null`` clears it. The rate is carried at three
decimals (a fourth is refused, never rounded); the ratio is a fraction in [0, 1]; the instalment day
is the 1st or the 30th; the lock is 7 or 14 days; the first instalment falls after the value date.

VersionDiffResponse.title: VersionDiffResponse
VersionDiffResponse.description:
Field-level deltas between two versions, grouped by section.

Every compared field is returned, changed or not — the compare modal renders
unchanged rows too and highlights from `old_value != new_value` client-side.

WaiveConditionRequest.title: WaiveConditionRequest
WaiveConditionRequest.description:
Waive an approval condition in one step (Milestone 1 Rule 06 §2.2.7, K6 — US-1.98).

The comment is optional, as on the prototype's "Are you sure?" dialog; a blank one is stored as
none. No expiry and no second approver: the waiver is a factual entry like a settlement.

app__modules__cases__interfaces__http__s.title: CollateralResponse
app__modules__cases__interfaces__http__s.description:
The DAT collateral of a financing's package (P29-06): kind, current total, an open proposal,
evidence, re-check state (+ who did which act, by name) and the full version history (every value
kept). The platform holds status + document only — no valuation, no per-object value, no rating
grade.

app__modules__contracts__interfaces__htt.title: CollateralResponse
app__modules__contracts__interfaces__htt.description: A collateral added to a contract (PRD1042-2167).
